lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: This is the Multiverse Broadcast Authority. A dimensional storm is crossing the band.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: Listeners may experience static, crosstalk, and brief exposure to other people's Tuesdays.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: Please stay tuned. Please hold on to something. A chair is fine.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: This is Dale Quarterly, with a storm bulletin, on whatever station this is. Winds are gusting at forty realities an hour. Kim is standing in it.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: I'm standing in it, Dale! Somebody's just handed me a kite!

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: It isn't my kite, Dale! It—

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Thank you, Kim. That was Kim. More at eleven.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: All drivers, all drivers. Storm's coming through the crossroads. Pull over, put the kettle on, and wait it out.

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: Rosalind, the road's gone sideways again.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Then drive sideways, love. Slowly. Ten and two.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: And this next one, my friends, is a—

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: He's run out of the stadium and into a completely—

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Your call is important to us in every—

lines.speaker: The Counter
lines.text: Seven. Seven—

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: I'm told we're back. Where was I. Ah, yes. A real heartbreaker.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Skip Daley here, blown onto your station with a storm update, and folks, it's a big one!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Scattered Tuesdays, heavy static, and a ninety percent chance of hearing somebody else's radio show! Isn't it great!

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: This is Captain Hum. Passing through. The whales are fine.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Thanks, Captain! The whales are fine, everybody!

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Hello, love. I'm not sure whose station this is. The storm's blown me in. It happens.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: While I'm here. Whatever's rattling tonight, it'll settle. Storms always think they're the whole sky.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: They never are.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Octavia Lowe, a long way from the club. The storm has carried me off, piano stool and all.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Listen to it, though. All that thunder and nobody keeping time. It's the best solo I've heard in years.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Hold on to your hats, darlings. Not mine. Mine's gone.

lines.speaker: Emergency Multiverse Broadcast System
lines.text: This is a test of the Emergency Multiverse Broadcast System. Every station in every reality is broadcasting this message, at the same time.

lines.speaker: Emergency Multiverse Broadcast System
lines.text: This has been a test. In an actual emergency, you would have been told what to do. It would have been, stay calm, and put the kettle on.

lines.speaker: Emergency Multiverse Broadcast System
lines.text: This is a test of the system that tests the Emergency Multiverse Broadcast System.

lines.speaker: Emergency Multiverse Broadcast System
lines.text: If you can hear this, the test is working. If you cannot hear this, please let us know.

lines.speaker: Emergency Multiverse Broadcast System
lines.text: This is not a test.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: This is an actual emergency. Somebody has left a very large casserole on the steps of the Multiverse Broadcast Authority, with no note.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: If this is your casserole, please collect it. It's lovely. We've had some.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: In the event of an actual multiverse emergency, listeners are advised to stay where they are, and who they are.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: Avoid meeting yourself. If you do meet yourself, be polite, and do not both reach for the door at once.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: You have reached the Emergency Multiverse Broadcast System. Your emergency is important to us.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: You are currently number four billion in the queue. Please stay on the line. An emergency will be with you shortly.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you for your patience.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We interrupt this programme, wherever you are, for the Emergency Multiverse Broadcast System test.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Which is, for the record, the most exciting thing to happen in my studio since eleven o'clock.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Which was a moment ago. It is always eleven.

lines.speaker: DJ Eventually
lines.text: So, the next one—

lines.speaker: DJ Eventually
lines.text: Do you hear that?

lines.speaker: DJ Eventually
lines.text: No. Me neither.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Good evening. Before we continue, I have been asked to say that nothing happened just now.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: I was asked by myself. Nothing happened. Here is the news.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Well.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: That was a real heartbreaker, wasn't it.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: I don't know what that was. Let's not. Here's a song.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And we're back, folks! Nothing happened! Absolutely nothing happened, and nobody heard anything!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: I heard it.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Doug.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: I'm just saying. I heard it.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: We don't, Doug. We don't.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: A short notice from the Hole Committee. The sound you may have heard just now was not the hole. The hole does not make sounds.

lines.speaker: Maureen Pettigrew
lines.text: Councillor Dibbs has asked me to stress this. He stressed it very hard. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Right. Let's.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Let's not, love.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Let's just have the next call. Who've we got? Lovely. Go on.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Case file. Earlier tonight, every frequency fell silent, and a low hum was heard in all known dimensions.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: No suspects. No motive. Nobody will discuss it. Case closed.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: It is the first case I have ever closed. I would rather not talk about why.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Good evening. This is Dale Quarterly, and this is not my newsroom.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: There is no desk. There is a great deal of music. Very well. I shall read the news over it.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The news is, I appear to be somewhere else. More at eleven.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Chip Thunderbuckle here, folks, and I have woken up on a completely different station, and I do not know the rules!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Here comes a song now! It's moving left! It's moving right! It's going for the chorus!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: I'm told it's just a song. Folks, it's just a song! What a game!

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Hello, love. Grenda here. I don't know how I've ended up on this station, but the lines appear to be open, so.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: If you're listening, and you've been meaning to ring someone, ring them. That's the advice.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: That's the whole show, really. Back to whoever lives here.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you for listening to this station, which is not my station. Your listening is important to us.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: You are caller number one. You are the only caller.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Please hold.

lines.speaker: Sir Reginald Thistlewood
lines.text: I have no idea where I am. But hush, now. Look.

lines.speaker: Sir Reginald Thistlewood
lines.text: Here, in the dim glow of a console, we find one of the rarest creatures in the multiverse. The night shift operator.

lines.speaker: Sir Reginald Thistlewood
lines.text: It is holding a mug with both hands. Remarkable. Let us not startle it.

lines.speaker: The Counter
lines.text: This is not Numbers Station Omega. Stand by.

lines.speaker: The Counter
lines.text: Song. Song. Advert. Song.

lines.speaker: The Counter
lines.text: We are doing our best. You still owe us geese.

lines.speaker: Chaz Brightley
lines.text: Hello and welcome to, oh! This isn't my studio! Where's my podium? Who's this?

lines.speaker: Shelley Shellbourne
lines.text: Hello. This is. Shelley.

lines.speaker: Chaz Brightley
lines.text: Shelley! Lovely! Quick question, Shelley, for ten points! Where are we?

lines.speaker: Shelley Shellbourne
lines.text: I'll get back to you.

lines.speaker: Chaz Brightley
lines.text: Take all the time you need! Folks, she's taking all the time she needs!

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: Hello. Hello. We have been listening to you for a very long time.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: Your programmes are very good. We especially like the adverts for ladders.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: We do not have ladders here. We do not have up.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: This is a message for every frequency at once. Do not be alarmed.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: We are only calling to say, we can hear you. All of you, at the same time.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: It is very loud. It is wonderful. Please keep going.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: Greetings from beyond the dial. We have received your signal, and we have a question.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: What is a Tuesday? Many of your stations mention it. Some of them seem worried.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: Reply at your convenience.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: Attention. We are the listeners on the far side. We have listened to your news since it began.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: We have one question. Is it ever not eleven.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: Thank you. That is all.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: This message is for Bev. Bev. We have found your song.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: It goes. Da. Da. Dum. Da. Da.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: It is—

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: Hello, small ship. Yes. You. The one with the amber light, and the kettle.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: We see you there, listening to the gaps. Nobody listens to the gaps.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: Thank you. Goodnight.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: Hello. We are the static. We are every voice that ever went out on the radio and was not heard.

lines.speaker: Unknown Signal
lines.text: We are fine. We are having a nice time. We only wanted you to know.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Good evening. Here is the news. The moon is near.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Good evening. Here is the news. The moon is nearer.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: I have the strangest feeling I've said that. It doesn't matter. More at eleven.

lines.speaker: Velocity Jones
lines.text: This next track is totally rad, and it's from—

lines.speaker: Velocity Jones
lines.text: This next track is totally rad, and it's from the future, which is now the past, which is also rad.

lines.speaker: Velocity Jones
lines.text: Everything's rad. Time is rad. Hi again!

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Ah. We seem to have slipped. Don't worry. I've been here before.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Everything that happens in the next minute turns out fine. I know. I was there.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Well. Here.

lines.speaker: Johnny Mirror
lines.text: And a one, and a two, and a

lines.speaker: Ynnhoj
lines.text: And a one, and a two, and a

lines.speaker: Johnny Mirror
lines.text: Ynnhoj. You went first.

lines.speaker: Ynnhoj
lines.text: You went first.

lines.speaker: Johnny Mirror
lines.text: Did I?

lines.speaker: Ynnhoj
lines.text: Did I?

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: You are experiencing a time slip. The last minute will now be repeated. Please enjoy it more this time.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: You are experiencing a time slip. The last minute will now be repeated. Please enjoy it even more this time.

lines.speaker: Shelley Shellbourne
lines.text: Oh. A time slip. Don't worry, everyone.

lines.speaker: Shelley Shellbourne
lines.text: I'm still on the same word as before.

lines.speaker: DJ Eventually
lines.text: So I was going to say something really important, and

lines.speaker: DJ Eventually
lines.text: So I was going to say something really important, and

lines.speaker: DJ Eventually
lines.text: Nope. Gone again. Twice now. That's a record.
